div.head: II As 6
div.ab: [Be wiccecræftum.] And we cwedon be ðam wiccecræftum ⁊ be lyblacum ⁊ morðdædum, gyf ðær man acweald wære, ⁊ he his ætsacan [B ends; Liebermann continues with Ld] ne mæge, þæt he beo his feores scyldig.
Be wiccecræftum. Ond we cwædon be þam wiccecræftum ⁊ be liblacum ⁊ be morðdædum, gif mon þær acweald wære, ⁊ he his ætsacan ne mihte, þæt he beo his feores scyldig.
Be wiccecræftum ⁊ liblacum. We cwædon be þam wiccecræftum ⁊ liblacum ⁊ morðdædum, gif þær mon acweald wære, ⁊ he his oðsacan ne mæg, þæt he beo his feores scyldig.
De sortilegis et liblacis. Decreuimus etiam de sortilegis et liblacis et mortem dantibus, si hominem occidant et negare non possint, uitę suę culpa iudicetur.
Be wiccecræftum. Ond we cwædon be þam wiccecræftum ⁊ be liblacum ⁊ be morðdædum, gif mon þær acweald wære, ⁊ he his ætsacan ne mihte, þæt he beo his feores scyldig.
And we have declared with regard to witchcraft and sorceries and deadly spells, if death is occasioned thereby, and [the accused] cannot deny it [the charge], that he shall forfeit his life.

Concerning witchcrafts. And we have pronounced concerning witchcrafts and sorceries and secret attempts on life, that, if anyone is killed by such, and he [the accused] cannot deny it, he is to forfeit his life.

Von Zauberkünsten (und Verhexungen. So). Und wir bestimmten über die Zauberkünste und über Verhexungen und über verstohlene Lebensgefährdungen, wenn ein Mensch dadurch getödtet wird, und der [Verklagte] es [überhaupt] nicht leugnen kann, dass er sein Leben verwirkt habe.

Of witchcraft (and sorcery. So). And we determined concerning witchcraft and sorcery and secret attempts on life, if a person is killed by them and the [accused] cannot deny it [at all], that he shall have forfeited his life.
div.note: B breaks off after ‘ætsacan’ at the end of a quire (the following leaves are lost; Af 3 follows in B); Liebermann continues with Ld. Liebermann compares EGu 11.
literally, “murders”. Open killing was not regarded as murder in Anglo-Saxon law.
